children.text: akāro vāsudevaḥ syād ākāraś ca pitāmahaḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'a' denotes <s>Vāsudeva</s>; the syllable 'ā' denotes the Grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>, i.e., <s>Brahmā</s>);

children.text: pūjāyām api māṅgalye ākāraḥ parikīrttitaḥ // PEk_1
children.translated_text: the syllable 'ā' is also proclaimed in the sense of worship and auspiciousness. (1)

children.text: ikāro ucyate kāmo lakṣmī rīkāra ucyate /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'i' is said to mean desire (<s>Kāma</s>); the syllable 'ī' denotes <s>Lakṣmī</s>;

children.text: ukāraḥ śaṅkaraḥ prokta ūkāraś cāpi rakṣaṇe // PEk_2
children.translated_text: the syllable 'u' is declared to be <s>Śaṅkara</s>; and the syllable 'ū' [is used] in the sense of protection. (2)

children.text: ṛkāro devamātā syād ṝkāro danujaprasūḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'ṛ' denotes the Mother of the Gods (<s>Devamātā</s>); the syllable 'ṝ' denotes the Mother of Demons (<s>Danujaprasū</s>);

children.text: ḷkāro devayoniḥ syāl ḹr mātā sadbhir ucyate // PEk_3
children.translated_text: the syllable 'ḷ' denotes the Divine Womb (<s>Devayoni</s>); the syllable 'ḹ' is said by the learned to mean 'mother.' (3)

children.text: ekāraḥ kathito viṣṇur aikāraś ca maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'e' is said to be <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the syllable 'ai' is <s>Maheśvara</s>;

children.text: okāras tu bhaved brahmā aukāro rudra ucyate // PEk_4
children.translated_text: the syllable 'o' is <s>Brahmā</s>; the syllable 'au' is said to be <s>Rudra</s>. (4)

children.text: aṃ syāc ca paramaṃ brahma aḥ syād devo maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'aṃ' denotes the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>; the syllable 'aḥ' denotes the god <s>Maheśvara</s>;

children.text: kaḥ prajāpatir uddiṣṭo ko vāyur iti śabditaḥ // PEk_5
children.translated_text: the syllable 'ka' is designated as <s>Prajāpati</s>; 'ka' is also the word for wind (<s>Vāyu</s>). (5)

children.text: kaś cātmā ca samākhyātaḥ kaḥ prakāśa udāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ka' is also proclaimed as the self (<s>Ātman</s>); 'ka' is cited as light (<s>prakāśa</s>);

children.text: kaṃ śiro jalam ākhyātaṃ kaṃ sukhaṃ ca prakīrtitam // PEk_6
children.translated_text: 'kaṃ' is said to be the head; 'kaṃ' is declared to be water; and 'kaṃ' is proclaimed as happiness. (6)

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ kuḥ samākhyātā kutsāyāṃ kuḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ku' is proclaimed in the sense of earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>); 'ku' is proclaimed in the sense of contempt (<s>kutsā</s>);

children.text: kham indriyaṃ samākhyātaṃ kham ākāśam udāhṛtam // PEk_7
children.translated_text: 'kha' is said to be a sense-organ (<s>indriya</s>); 'kha' is cited as space (<s>ākāśa</s>). (7)

children.text: khaṃ svarge ca samākhyātaṃ khaṃ sarpe ca prakīrtitaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Kha' is said to be heaven (<s>svarga</s>); 'kha' is proclaimed in the sense of a serpent;

children.text: tathā śvabhre ca khaṃ prāhuḥ khaṃ śūnye ca prakīrttitam // PEk_8
children.translated_text: likewise, 'kha' is said for a pit or hole; and 'kha' is proclaimed for emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>). (8)

children.text: go gaṇapatir uddiṣṭo go gandharvaḥ prakīrttitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Go' designates <s>Gaṇapati</s>; 'go' is proclaimed as a <s>Gandharva</s>;

children.text: gaṃ gītaṃ gā ca gāthā syād gaur dhenur gauḥ sarasvatī // PEk_9
children.translated_text: 'gaṃ' is a song; 'gā' is a verse (<s>gāthā</s>); 'gau' is a cow (<s>dhenu</s>); 'gau' is <s>Sarasvatī</s>. (9)

children.text: gaur mātāpi samuddiṣṭā pṛthivyāṃ gauḥ prakīrttitā /
children.translated_text: 'Gau' is also designated as a mother; 'gau' is proclaimed in the sense of earth;

children.text: gho ghaṇṭāyāṃ samākhyātaḥ kiṅkiṇī ghā prakīrttitā // PEk_10
children.translated_text: 'gho' is said to mean a bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>); 'ghā' is proclaimed as a small bell (<s>kiṅkiṇī</s>). (10)

children.text: upamā ghā samākhyātā kusvare ghuḥ prakīrttitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ghā' is said to mean a simile (<s>upamā</s>); 'ghu' is proclaimed for a bad sound;

children.text: hanane ghā samākhyātā gandhane ghaḥ prakīrttitaḥ // PEk_11
children.translated_text: 'ghā' is said in the sense of killing; 'gha' is proclaimed in the sense of smelling. (11)

children.text: ṅakāro bhairavaḥ khyāto ṅakāro viṣaye smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'ṅa' is known as <s>Bhairava</s>; the syllable 'ṅa' is remembered in the sense of an object;

children.text: cakāraś candramāḥ khyātas taskaraś ca prakīrttitaḥ // PEk_12
children.translated_text: the syllable 'ca' is known as the moon (<s>Candramā</s>); and it is also proclaimed as a thief (<s>taskara</s>). (12)

children.text: nirmalaṃ chaṃ samākhyātaṃ taraṇī chaḥ prakīrttitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Cha' is said to mean purity (<s>nirmala</s>); 'cha' is proclaimed as a boat (<s>taraṇī</s>);

children.text: chedane chaḥ samākhyāto vidvadbhiḥ śabdakovidaiḥ // PEk_13
children.translated_text: 'cha' is said in the sense of cutting, by the learned, the experts in words. (13)

children.text: vegite jaḥ samākhyāto jaghane jaḥ prakīrttitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ja' is said in the sense of speed; 'ja' is proclaimed in the sense of the hip;

children.text: jetā ca jaḥ samākhyātaḥ prasiddhaiḥ śabdakovidaiḥ // PEk_14
children.translated_text: 'ja' is also said to mean a conqueror, by the well-known experts in words. (14)

children.text: jhaṃjhāvāte jhakāraḥ syān naṣṭe jhaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'jha' denotes a whirlwind (<s>jhañjhāvāta</s>); 'jha' is cited in the sense of destruction;

children.text: ñakāro gāyane prokto ñakāro ghargharadhvanau // PEk_15
children.translated_text: the syllable 'ña' is declared in the sense of singing; the syllable 'ña' [is used] for a gurgling sound. (15)

children.text: ṭaṅkāre ṭaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ṭā ṭo dhvanau ca prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ṭa' [is used] for a clinking sound; 'ṭā' for earth; 'ṭo' is proclaimed for a sound;

children.text: ṭho maheśvara ākhyātaḥ śūnye ca ṭhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ // PEk_16
children.translated_text: 'ṭho' is declared to be <s>Maheśvara</s>; and 'ṭha' is proclaimed in the sense of emptiness. (16)

children.text: bṛhaddhvanau ca ṭhaḥ proktas tathā candrasya maṇḍale /
children.translated_text: 'Ṭha' is declared for a loud sound, and likewise for the disc of the moon;

children.text: ḍakāraḥ śaṅkaraḥ proktas trāsadhvanyoḥ prakīrtitaḥ // PEk_17
children.translated_text: the syllable 'ḍa' is declared to be <s>Śaṅkara</s>; it is proclaimed for terror and for sound. (17)

children.text: ḍhakāraḥ kīrtitā ḍhakkā nirguṇe ca dhvanāv api /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'ḍha' is proclaimed as a drum (<s>ḍhakkā</s>), and also for a sound without quality;

children.text: ṇakāraḥ kīrtito jñāne nirṇaye 'pi prakīrtitaḥ // PEk_18
children.translated_text: the syllable 'ṇa' is proclaimed in the sense of knowledge and also in the sense of ascertainment. (18)

children.text: takāraḥ kathitaś cauraḥ kroḍe pucche prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'ta' is said to be a thief; it is proclaimed in the sense of tail and lap;

children.text: śiloccaye thakāraḥ syāt thakāro bhayarakṣaṇe // PEk_19
children.translated_text: the syllable 'tha' is used for a rocky mountain; and 'tha' for fear and protection. (19)

children.text: daṃ kalatre samākhyātaṃ do dānacchedadhātuṣu /
children.translated_text: 'Daṃ' is said in the sense of a wife (<s>kalatra</s>); 'do' [is used] in the verbal roots of giving and cutting;

children.text: dhaṃ dhane ca dhaneśe dho dhā dhātari nidarśitaḥ // PEk_20
children.translated_text: 'dhaṃ' [is used] for wealth and for the Lord of Wealth (<s>Dhaneśa</s>); 'dho' and 'dhā' are indicated for the sustainer (<s>dhātṛ</s>). (20)

children.text: dhiṣaṇā dhīḥ samākhyātā dhūś ca syād bhāracintayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Intelligence (<s>dhiṣaṇā</s>) is said to be 'dhī'; and 'dhū' is used for burden and thought;

children.text: nakāraḥ sugate bandhe nuḥ stutau ca prakīrtitaḥ // PEk_21
children.translated_text: the syllable 'na' [is used] for the <s>Sugata</s> (<s>Buddha</s>) and for binding; 'nu' is proclaimed in the sense of praise. (21)

children.text: netā nīś ca samākhyātas taraṇau nauḥ prakīrtitā /
children.translated_text: 'Nī' is said to mean a leader; and in the sense of a boat, 'nau' is proclaimed;

children.text: nakāraḥ saugate buddhau stuto sūrye ca kīrtitaḥ // PEk_22
children.translated_text: the syllable 'na' in the Buddhist sense means awakening (<s>buddhi</s>); praised, it is also proclaimed for the sun. (22)

children.text: naśabdaḥ svāgate bandhau vṛkṣe sūrye ca kīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'na' [is used] for welcome, for binding, for a tree, and is proclaimed for the sun;

children.text: paḥ kuberaḥ samākhyātaḥ paścime ca prakīrtitaḥ // PEk_23
children.translated_text: 'pa' is said to be <s>Kubera</s>; and is proclaimed for the west. (23)

children.text: pavane paḥ samākhyātaḥ pāḥ pāne pāś ca pātari /
children.translated_text: 'Pa' is said in the sense of wind; 'pā' for drinking; and 'pā' for a protector;

children.text: kaphe vāte phakāraḥ syāt tathāhvāne prakīrtitaḥ // PEk_24
children.translated_text: the syllable 'pha' is used for phlegm and for wind; and likewise is proclaimed for a call. (24)

children.text: jhaṃjhāvāte phakāraḥ syād akṣare ca prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The syllable 'pha' is used for a whirlwind; and is proclaimed for a syllable (<s>akṣara</s>);

children.text: kope phiś ca samākhyātas tathā niṣphalabhāṣaṇe // PEk_25
children.translated_text: 'phi' is said in the sense of anger; and likewise in the sense of fruitless speech. (25)

children.text: vakṣaḥsthale ca baḥ prokto gadāyāṃ samudāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ba' is declared for the chest; it is cited in the sense of a mace (<s>gadā</s>);

children.text: nakṣatraṃ bhaṃ budhaiḥ proktaṃ bhramare bhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ // PEk_26
children.translated_text: 'bhaṃ' is declared by the wise as a constellation (<s>nakṣatra</s>); 'bha' is proclaimed for a bee (<s>bhramara</s>). (26)

children.text: bhā dīptir api bhūr bhūmir bhīr bhayaṃ kathitā budhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Bhā' [means] radiance; 'bhū' [means] earth; 'bhī' [means] fear, as stated by the wise;

children.text: maḥ śivaś candramā vedhā mā ca lakṣmīḥ prakīrtitā // PEk_27
children.translated_text: 'ma' [means] <s>Śiva</s>, the moon, or the Creator (<s>Vedhā</s>); and 'mā' is proclaimed as <s>Lakṣmī</s>. (27)
